bundestag.summary:
SUMMARY:
This document is the stenographic report of the 78th session of the 21st legislative period of the German Bundestag, held on Friday, May 8, 2026. The session covered a range of agenda topics. A significant portion of the discussion revolved around Agenda Item 22, concerning the second and third readings of a government bill to introduce electronic monitoring of residence and perpetrator work within the Protection against Violence Act. This item also included a recommendation from the Committee on Budget Affairs and a report from the Committee on Legal Affairs and Consumer Protection regarding a motion by Die Linke for a comprehensive strategy against domestic and gender-based violence, rather than isolated measures. Several MPs, including Carmen Wegge (SPD), Rainer Galla (AfD), Dr. Günter Krings (CDU/CSU), Dr. Lena Gumnior (Bündnis 90/Die Grünen), Aaron Valent (Die Linke), and Tobias Matthias Peterka (AfD), contributed to this debate. Federal Minister Dr. Stefanie Hubig (BMJV) also addressed the chamber on this topic.

Other agenda items included Agenda Item 23, which featured the first reading of a bill by the AfD to abolish the Wind Energy Area Requirement Act, and a related AfD motion for a nationwide moratorium on wind industry expansion. This led to discussions involving Christian Reck (AfD), Dr. Maria-Lena Weiss (CDU/CSU), Katrin Uhlig (Bündnis 90/Die Grünen), and Dr. Paul Schmidt (AfD), among others. Agenda Item 24 focused on a motion by the CDU/CSU and SPD regarding the "Day of Urban Development Funding 2026" as a driver for strong cities and municipalities. Finally, Agenda Item 25 encompassed several motions by Die Linke aimed at strengthening works council rights, improving their working conditions, promoting their establishment, and enhancing employee participation in the workplace, including on a multinational level through reforms of European Works Councils. Speakers in this segment included Cem Ince (Die Linke), Peter Aumer (CDU/CSU), Pascal Meiser (Die Linke), Hans-Jürgen Goßner (AfD), Angelika Glöckner (SPD), and Ricarda Lang (Bündnis 90/Die Grünen).

UKRAINIAN MEN:
No discussion about Ukrainian men found in this session.

facts.fact: During the French Revolution, the radical Jacobins promoted a style of dress called 'sans-culottes,' which literally meant 'without knee-breeches.' This was a deliberate rejection of the aristocratic fashion of wearing tight silk or linen breeches that reached the knee, symbolizing their opposition to the monarchy and the old regime. The sans-culottes favored long trousers, a symbol of the working class.

The 'Great Emu War' of 1932 was a bizarre episode where the Australian military, armed with machine guns, was deployed to cull a population of emus that were destroying crops in Western Australia. The operation was largely unsuccessful, with the emus proving to be surprisingly elusive and resilient. The 'war' was a source of national amusement and embarrassment, and the military eventually withdrew.
